SPARK LAB / PATTERNS & APPLICATIONS / V1.1

More ways
to make a spark.

Four directions for the lab’s workshops, projects and everyday work. Compare the pattern colourways and see where each one is most useful.

Explore repeating arrows: scale, density and colour ↗

Titles shown below are design examples. Dates, times, names and locations remain placeholders. Editable originals are in the brand kit.

Arrows

One arrow. Many possibilities.

The source arrow repeats at small, medium and oversized scales. Mix eight directions in a modular grid, scatter arrows freely, follow crossing streams or combine the arrow with the original spark. Try the interactive explorer for scale, density and colour controls.

Signal

Make an announcement.

The original arrow becomes a set of expanding outlines. A single orange contour gives the field a point of focus. Best for workshops, open sessions and short headlines.

Connections

Show how an idea develops.

Routes cross a quiet registration grid and meet at visible junctions. Use it for research, collaboration, project stories and working documents.

Layers

Let the material lead.

Nested contours suggest toolpaths, sections and additive manufacturing. The irregular shape gives covers and small printed pieces a softer, more tactile character.
